sections.content: You know *ir a* + infinitive from A1 Unit 25 ("going to"), *estar* + gerund from A1 Unit 19 and *poco a poco* from A2 Unit 28. *Ir* + gerund is a different pattern: there is no *a*, and the verb after it is a gerund. It says that something moves forward step by step instead of happening all at once: *Voy aprendiendo* is "I'm gradually picking it up". It goes very well with *poco a poco* and with *a medida que* (B1 Unit 2). *Ir* can be in any tense: *voy aprendiendo*, *iba aprendiendo*, *fui aprendiendo*. With a reflexive verb, the pronoun goes before *ir*: *El barrio se iba llenando de tiendas*.
sections.title: Gradual progress
ir + gerund
rows: Poco a poco voy entendiendo mejor el español.
Little by little I am coming to understand Spanish better.
A medida que pasaban los días, íbamos conociendo a los vecinos.
As the days went by, we got to know the neighbours little by little.
El barrio se fue llenando de tiendas nuevas.
The neighbourhood gradually filled up with new shops.
El proyecto va avanzando a buen ritmo.
The project is moving forward at a good pace.

sections.content: *Voy a estudiar* and *Voy estudiando* look alike, but they mean different things. With *a* + infinitive it is a plan ("I am going to study"); without *a*, and with a gerund, it is gradual progress ("I am studying as I go"). In the past, *se iba llenando* shows the change while it was happening, and *se fue llenando* sums it up as one finished change.
